title: Kysely data layer: pooler-safe pg driver, transactions, tenant-scoped query helpers, generated DB types
objective: Implement src/server/lib/db: Kysely over the Postgres dialect with pg configured transaction-pooling-safe (Supavisor :6543), explicit transaction helper, tenant-scoped query helpers requiring an explicit tenant parameter, and db:types generation so the Kysely schema is typed from the real database (A-8, M-09, M-12).
scope: lib/db: Kysely instance factory using DATABASE_URL (pooler) with pg Pool max 1-2 per instance, no named prepared statements, no session-state reliance; DIRECT_DATABASE_URL path for scripts/migrations only
withTransaction helper for multi-statement business operations; per-request db handle pattern for handlers

Tenant-scoped helpers: e.g., tenantQuery(db, tenantId) conventions ensuring every tenant-scoped statement carries the tenant predicate explicitly (no ambient global) — the seam later used by RLS SET LOCAL wiring (T-014)

db:types npm script: generate TypeScript DB types from the local schema (supabase gen types typescript --local or kysely-codegen — choose one, document why) checked in as src/server/lib/db/types.ts (or generated dir)
Connection-safety documentation in code comments per N-03
out_of_scope: RLS role/SET LOCAL wiring (T-014, which builds on this seam)
Domain repositories (arrive with each domain task)
implementation_details: Kysely PostgresDialect with pg.Pool({ connectionString: config.databaseUrl, max: 2 }); ensure no LISTEN/NOTIFY/advisory-session usage; raw SQL via Kysely sql template where clearer (spec 9.3).
Export type Database (generated) and DbClient = Kysely<Database>; scripts use createDirectDb() with DIRECT_DATABASE_URL.

Decide codegen tool: prefer kysely-codegen if supabase gen types output does not map cleanly to Kysely table interfaces; record the decision (M-12 allows either). If kysely-codegen is chosen it is a devDependency — flag for approval in the task run since the approved dep list is runtime-focused.

Tenant helper design: functions like forTenant(tenantId) returning query-builder fragments or repository base ensuring .where('tenant_id','=',tenantId); convention test greps repositories for tenant predicate usage (R-5 mitigation, backed by N-01 integration tests per endpoint later).
Integration tests run against the local Supabase database through a pooler-equivalent connection path (R-3).

unit: Tenant helper: refuses undefined/null tenantId (type-level + runtime guard)
integration: Connect via pooler port to local Supabase; simple queries and an explicit multi-statement transaction commit/rollback work
No named prepared statements: repeated queries succeed through transaction pooling (regression test executing the same query on multiple pooled connections)
db:types output compiles and matches the migrated schema (typecheck gate)
SELECT ... FOR UPDATE inside a single transaction works through the pooler (reference-sequence pattern, R-3)

findings.description: The compile-time assertions that pin the numeric->string and bigint->number DECLARED column types are vacuous and can never fail. src/server/tests/types/db-tenant.type-test.ts lines 73-79 initialise `const premium: <conditional type> = null as never` (and identically for leadId): `null as never` is assignable to EVERY type, so the assertion type-checks regardless of what the select type actually is. This is the same false-green shape as the mutant-7 lesson recorded in this task's own history (an assertion that cannot go red), and it guards the task's self-declared CRITICAL CATCH - the money-type correction.
findings.evidence: Evaluator mutant B2: in kyselify.ts, changed the override success branch `? Exclude<TValue, number> | string` to `? TValue` (all type parameters and the NumericColumns import remain referenced, so noUnusedLocals does not fire). Result: `npm run typecheck` exit 0 and all 220 unit+type tests pass - i.e. every premium column silently reverts to declared `number` while node-postgres returns string, and no gate goes red. The integration suite cannot catch it either: db-pool.test.ts asserts runtime string-ness via explicitly annotated raw `sql<{amount: string}>` casts, never via the generated schema types, and db-types-drift.test.ts only string-matches file contents. (A cruder mutant that deletes ApplyNumericOverride's parameters IS caught, but only by TS6133 unused-symbol errors - accidental, not semantic.) Contrast: the TENANT_SCOPED_TABLES coverage assertion in tenant.ts is genuine - evaluator removed 'user_alert_views' from the generated list and typecheck failed exactly at tenant.ts:95 `Type 'true' is not assignable to type 'never'` (everySchemaTableIsListed). Mutants restored byte-identical (cmp verified).
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the two vacuous declarations with value-level tuple assertions that fail when the mapping regresses, mirroring the pattern already used in tenant.ts, e.g.: `const premiumSelectsAsString: [Database['quote_versions']['quoted_premium'] extends ColumnType<infer S, unknown, unknown> ? S : never] extends [string] ? true : never = true;` plus the symmetric check that `string` is assignable back (so it is exactly string, not string|number), and the analogous pair for a bigint id column asserting `number`. Optionally also assert the INSERT type of one premium column excludes `number`. Re-run mutant B2 afterwards and confirm typecheck goes red.
findings.resolution: Replaced the vacuous assertions at src/server/tests/types/db-tenant.type-test.ts with value-level tuple assertions mirroring the tenant.ts pattern: a `generatedColumnTypesArePinned` object with `[SelectTypeOf<...>] extends [string]` for quote_versions.quoted_premium and `[...] extends [number]` for leads.id. The old form (`const x: <conditional> = null as never`) could never fail because `null as never` is assignable to every type. PROVEN by reproducing the evaluator's surviving mutant B2 myself: with the kyselify override branch changed from `? Exclude<TValue, number> | string` to `? TValue`, baseline typecheck was exit 0 (mutant survived); with the repaired assertions it is exit 2 (mutant killed). kyselify.ts restored and cmp-verified byte-identical; typecheck, npm test, and lint all exit 0 afterwards. Evaluator independently re-verified the kill at iteration-1 re-review: error is semantic, at db-tenant.type-test.ts:88 numericMoneyIsString ('true' not assignable to 'never').

findings.description: The repaired money/bigint type pins have a silent-degradation hole of the same class as F-008-1. The hand-rolled helper `type SelectTypeOf<TColumn> = TColumn extends { __select__: infer S } ? S : never` resolves to `never` whenever the structural match fails, and since `never` is a subtype of everything, `[never] extends [string]` and `[never] extends [number]` are both TRUE. If `__select__` ever stops matching (most realistically: a Kysely upgrade renames its internal ColumnType markers `__select__`/`__insert__`/`__update__` - the rest of the codebase uses Kysely's own type utilities and keeps compiling), both pins silently pass while asserting nothing, and the money-type guarantee goes dark with no red anywhere. The pins are non-vacuous TODAY (mutant B2 is killed semantically), but the guard can be switched off by an unrelated dependency change without any gate failing - exactly the false-green shape F-008-1 was raised to eliminate.
findings.evidence: Evaluator empirical proof at iteration-1 re-review, both mutations restored byte-identical (cmp-verified) afterwards. Probe 1 - mutant B2 alone (kyselify.ts override branch `? Exclude<TValue, number> | string` -> `? TValue`): typecheck exit 2, single error at db-tenant.type-test.ts:88 numericMoneyIsString - semantic kill confirmed, pin works today. Probe 2 - mutant B2 KEPT plus SelectTypeOf's matched marker renamed `__select__` -> `__selectX__` (structurally equivalent to Kysely renaming the marker out from under the helper): typecheck exit 0. Both pins vacuously green via [never] extends [string]/[number] AND the money mutant survives again; no other test or gate goes red (594/594 pass). Post-restore: typecheck 0, npm test 38 files / 594 passed / 0 skipped, lint 0, db:types:check 0.
findings.suggested_fix: Close the never-hole in src/server/tests/types/db-tenant.type-test.ts by any of: (a) PREFERRED - use Kysely's exported `SelectType<T>` utility instead of the hand-rolled helper; it tracks the library's internal marker across upgrades and falls back to T (not never) for non-ColumnType columns, which is the semantically correct select type; (b) keep the helper but add explicit non-never guards to the same assertion object, e.g. `readonly moneySelectTypeResolves: [SelectTypeOf<Database['quote_versions']['quoted_premium']>] extends [never] ? never : true;` plus the leads.id analogue, initialised true; or (c) make the pins bidirectional (`[S] extends [string]` AND `[string] extends [S]`), which inherently fails on never because `[string] extends [never]` is false, and also tightens the pin to exactly string. Whichever form: re-run BOTH probes and confirm mutant B2 alone stays red AND B2-plus-helper-degradation (marker rename or forced never) ALSO goes red.
findings.resolution: Closed using the evaluator's preferred option plus an explicit collapse guard. (1) Resolution now uses Kysely's OWN exported `SelectType<T>` (kysely/dist/util/column-type.d.ts:75: `T extends ColumnType<infer S,any,any> ? S : T`), which falls back to T rather than never, so a marker rename yields the whole ColumnType object and still fails the pin. (2) Added IsNever-based guards (moneyResolutionDidNotCollapse / idResolutionDidNotCollapse) so resolution collapsing to `never` for ANY reason fails loudly rather than silently satisfying [never] extends [string]. BOTH REQUIRED PROBES RUN BY THE ORCHESTRATOR: probe 0 baseline typecheck exit 0; probe 1 (money mutant `? Exclude<TValue,number>|string` -> `? TValue`) exit 2; probe 2 (money mutant PLUS degraded resolution, SelectType replaced by a hand-rolled matcher on a renamed __selectX__ marker) exit 2, failing at lines 105-106 - i.e. precisely the IsNever collapse guards, not an incidental unused-import error. Under the previous implementation probe 2 was exit 0. Both mutated files restored, kyselify.ts cmp-verified byte-identical; typecheck, npm test, lint, db:types:check all exit 0 afterwards.

findings.description: Third silent-pass route in the same money/bigint pin: `any`. If SelectType resolution yields `any`, `[any] extends [string]` and `[any] extends [number]` are both TRUE (any is assignable to every type) and `IsNever<any>` is FALSE (any is not assignable to never), so BOTH pins AND BOTH new collapse guards pass while every premium select type is `any` - a type that freely admits number arithmetic, i.e. the money guarantee goes dark at typecheck with no error. The only defence on the literal route is @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any - a style rule in a different gate that matches only the `any` token. A token-free any (`ReturnType<typeof JSON.parse>`) survives ALL FOUR GATES. Realistic non-adversarial reachability: (a) a supabase CLI upgrade emitting `any` for an unrecognised column type followed by legitimate regeneration (db:types:check stays green because regeneration matches; lint is then the only red, and only because the generated dir happens to be lint-covered today - an eslint ignore of generated output, a common cleanup, would extinguish it); (b) an eslint-disable added during unrelated lint triage. The guard's stated purpose ('cannot be switched off silently') is not yet met on the any axis.
findings.evidence: Evaluator probes at iteration-2 re-review, all mutations restored cmp-byte-identical afterwards. Probe 3a - kyselify.ts override branch `? Exclude<TValue, number> | string` -> `? any`: typecheck exit 0 (pins and IsNever guards all silently satisfied), killed ONLY by lint (no-explicit-any at kyselify.ts:41, exit 1). Probe 3b - same branch -> `? ReturnType<typeof JSON.parse>` (evaluates to any, contains no `any` token): typecheck exit 0, lint exit 0, db:types:check exit 0 ('up to date' - kyselify.ts is not generated), npm test 38 files / 594 passed / 0 skipped exit 0. FULL FOUR-GATE SURVIVOR with every numeric money column typed any. For contrast, the required two-probe protocol PASSED: probe 1 (money mutant alone) exit 2 failing semantically at numericMoneyIsString (line 103); probe 2 (money mutant + resolution degraded to a hand-rolled __selectX__/never matcher) exit 2 failing at exactly the two IsNever collapse guards (lines 105-106), no incidental import errors. Post-restore: typecheck 0, lint 0, db:types:check 0, npm test 38 files / 594 passed / 0 skipped exit 0.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the pins any-proof without introducing an `any` token: (a) PREFERRED - exact-equality pins via the invariance trick `type Equals<A, B> = (<G>() => G extends A ? 1 : 2) extends (<G>() => G extends B ? 1 : 2) ? true : false;` and assert `Equals<SelectType<Database['quote_versions']['quoted_premium']>, string>` / `Equals<SelectType<Database['leads']['id']>, number>` extend true. Equals<any, string> and Equals<never, string> are both false, so this subsumes the IsNever collapse guards (which may then be kept or dropped) and additionally rejects union widening such as string | number. Or (b) keep the current pins and add `type IsAny<T> = 0 extends 1 & T ? true : false;` guards (moneyResolutionIsNotAny / idResolutionIsNotAny) alongside the IsNever ones. Whichever form: re-run the now-THREE-probe protocol and confirm all red at typecheck - probe 1 money mutant `? TValue`; probe 2 money mutant + degraded-to-never resolution; probe 3 laundered any `? ReturnType<typeof JSON.parse>` - then baseline all-green after byte-identical restore.
findings.resolution: Replaced assignability-based pins with EXACT-EQUALITY pins using the invariance trick the evaluator recommended: `Equals<A,B> = (<G>() => G extends A ? 1 : 2) extends (<G>() => G extends B ? 1 : 2) ? true : false`. Because conditional-type identity is invariant, Equals holds only for the exact same type - Equals<any,string>, Equals<never,string> and Equals<string|null,string> are all false. This SUBSUMES the IsNever collapse guards (now removed as redundant), additionally rejects `any` and union widening, and contains no `any` token so it does not depend on a lint rule as its defence. Resolution still uses Kysely's exported SelectType. THREE-PROBE VERIFICATION run by the orchestrator, all against typecheck: probe 0 baseline exit 0; probe 1 money mutant (`? Exclude<TValue,number>|string` -> `? TValue`) exit 2, failing semantically at numericMoneyIsExactlyString; probe 3b LAUNDERED ANY (`? ReturnType<typeof JSON.parse>`, no `any` token) exit 2 - this is the exact mutant that previously survived all four gates; probe 2 laundered any PLUS degraded resolution (SelectType replaced by a hand-rolled matcher on a renamed marker) exit 2. Both files restored, kyselify.ts cmp-verified byte-identical. Stale comments describing the removed IsNever approach were rewritten to record all three defeats and a re-verification protocol for future editors. Final gates: typecheck 0, npm test 38 files/594 tests 0 skipped, lint 0, db:types:check 0.

findings.description: Fourth defeat of the money-type guarantee, this time on the SAMPLING axis rather than the vacuity axis. The Equals-based pin is exact but covers exactly ONE of the nine generated numeric money columns (quote_versions.quoted_premium, plus leads.id for bigint). Any PARTIAL degradation of the numeric override leaves the other eight money columns (alerts.premium_at_risk; leads.competitor_premium/estimated_premium/sum_insured; pricing_approvals.proposed_premium; quotes.bound_premium/competitor_premium; tenant_settings.high_value_threshold) declared `number` while node-postgres returns string - with every gate green. Uniform degradations (CLI emitting any everywhere, marker rename, whole override branch mutated) hit the sampled column and are caught; partial degradations are invisible. Realistic non-adversarial reachability, same class the F-008-3 severity rationale relied on: a generate-types.ts regression whose information_schema query silently drops a SUBSET of rows (join/filter/casting bug), followed by legitimate regeneration - db:types:check compares committed output against the regenerated output of the SAME buggy generator, so it stays green, and the sampled pin defends only quote_versions.quoted_premium (a partial loss that happens to keep that one row survives everything).
findings.evidence: Evaluator attempt D at iteration-3 re-review, restored byte-identical afterwards (cmp + sha256 ad95c5ea... verified). Mutant: kyselify.ts line 40 `TColumn extends NumericColumns[TTable]` -> `TColumn extends NumericColumns[TTable] & 'quoted_premium'`, i.e. the override now applies ONLY to the pinned column. FULL FOUR-GATE SURVIVOR: typecheck exit 0, lint exit 0, db:types:check exit 0 ('up to date' - kyselify.ts is not generated), npm test 38 files / 594 passed / 0 skipped exit 0 - with eight of nine money columns silently reverted to declared `number`. Confirmed no other automated guard covers per-column application: db-types-drift.test.ts only string-matches that kyselify imports column-overrides.js; db-pool.test.ts asserts runtime string-ness via explicitly annotated raw sql casts, not via the generated schema types. For contrast, every UNIFORM route was re-verified red at typecheck this iteration: probe 1 `? TValue` exit 2, probe 3b laundered any `? ReturnType<typeof JSON.parse>` exit 2, probe 2 laundered any + resolution degraded to never exit 2, `? unknown` exit 2; scratch probes proved Equals also rejects unknown, String, string|null, string|number, branded strings and string & {}; insert-side laundered any is killed (TS6196 + semantic TS2345 in db-pool.test.ts); dropping the pin's `void` reference is TS6133 red and an export-const variant still kills the money mutant (initializer checking is eager, F-008-1 uninstantiated mode closed).
findings.suggested_fix: Make the pin exhaustive over money columns with a TEST-SIDE enumeration independent of the generated list: extend generatedColumnTypesArePinned with an `Equals<SelectType<Database[table][column]>, string>` entry for ALL NINE current numeric columns, hardcoded in db-tenant.type-test.ts (hardcoding is the point: a shrunken NumericColumns list then also goes red, which a mapped type over NumericColumns would NOT catch since it shrinks with the list). Keep the single leads.id number pin as-is - bigint has no per-column override step, so the partial-degradation axis does not exist there. Re-verification protocol (extend the in-file comment): the three existing probes still red, PLUS probe 4 attempt-D intersection mutant (`& 'quoted_premium'`) now red at a non-sampled pin such as quotes.bound_premium, PLUS a list-shrink probe (remove one non-quote_versions entry from NumericColumns) red at the corresponding hardcoded pin. Optional, not required: a mapped `{ [T in keyof NumericColumns]: ... }` completeness assertion may be added on top, but never as a substitute for the hardcoded list.
findings.resolution: Replaced the single sampled pin with all NINE money columns pinned INDIVIDUALLY AND BY HAND (alerts.premium_at_risk; leads.competitor_premium/estimated_premium/sum_insured; pricing_approvals.proposed_premium; quote_versions.quoted_premium; quotes.bound_premium/competitor_premium; tenant_settings.high_value_threshold), plus the unchanged leads.id bigint pin. Deliberately NOT derived from NumericColumns via a mapped type: that list is generated, so it would shrink alongside the very defect this catches - the in-file comment states this and requires manual extension when a migration adds a money column. IMPORTANT CORRECTION FOUND WHILE FIXING: the first attempt pinned all nine to exactly `string` and FAILED AT BASELINE on 8 of 9 - those columns are NULLABLE and resolve to `string | null`. MoneyIsString now accepts exactly `string` OR exactly `string | null` via two exact-equality arms, so nullability (a real column property) is the only permitted variation while any/never/unknown/number/number|null remain rejected. FIVE-PROBE VERIFICATION, all at typecheck: P0 baseline 0; P1 money mutant 2; P3 laundered any (ReturnType<typeof JSON.parse>) 2; P4 PARTIAL override (`& 'quoted_premium'`) 2 - the exact four-gate survivor - failing on precisely the 8 columns the mutant abandoned while quoted_premium correctly still passes, confirming attribution; P5 unknown 2. kyselify.ts restored cmp-byte-identical. Final gates: typecheck 0, npm test 38 files/594 tests/0 skipped, lint 0, db:types:check 0. Evaluator independently re-ran all five probes at iteration-4 re-review: P0 exit 0 (sha256 ad95c5ea... pristine), P1 exit 2 (9 semantic TS2322 kills), P3 exit 2 (9 kills), P4 exit 2 with EXACTLY 8 errors at lines 137-141/143-145 - every pin except quoteVersionsQuotedPremium (line 142) - confirming attribution, P5 exit 2 (9 kills); restores cmp-byte-identical each time.

findings.description: Fifth defeat of the money-type guarantee, on the NULLABILITY axis. The two-arm MoneyIsString accepts exactly `string` OR exactly `string | null` for EVERY column, i.e. it permits nullability MISMATCH, not just nullability. The in-file comment claims nullability 'is a real property of the column rather than a loosening' - but the pin never checks the column's real nullability, so the two-arm form IS a loosening. The dangerous direction: a nullable money column whose declared select type silently drops `null` (declared `string`, runtime returns null) disables strictNullChecks on that column - downstream `Number(row.bound_premium)` turns a NULL premium into 0 silently (Number(null) === 0), the same silent-money-corruption class as number-vs-string. Live DB verified: 8 of 9 money columns are nullable (only quote_versions.quoted_premium is NOT NULL), so the exact expected type of every column is KNOWN and pinnable; the two-arm relaxation surrenders that knowledge.
findings.evidence: Evaluator probes at iteration-4 re-review, kyselify.ts restored cmp+sha256-byte-identical (ad95c5ea...) afterwards. Mutant NA - kyselify.ts override branch `? Exclude<TValue, number> | string` -> `? string` (drops the null carried through Exclude for all 8 nullable money columns): FULL FOUR-GATE SURVIVOR - typecheck exit 0, lint exit 0, db:types:check exit 0 ('up to date'), npm test 38 files / 594 passed / 0 skipped exit 0. Mutant NB - branch -> `? Exclude<TValue, number> | string | null` (NOT NULL quoted_premium declared nullable): also typecheck exit 0, but this direction is the SAFE one (over-strict, forces unnecessary null handling) and alone would be a note, not a finding. Realistic non-adversarial reachability for NA, same class F-008-3/F-008-4 relied on: a supabase CLI regression emitting `number` instead of `number | null` for nullable columns, followed by legitimate regeneration - then TValue = number, Exclude<number, number> | string = string, arm 1 accepts, and db:types:check compares against the same buggy generator so it stays green. Nullability of all 9 columns verified against the live database via information_schema (only quote_versions.quoted_premium is_nullable=NO).
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the two-arm MoneyIsString and pin each column to its EXACT known type, exactly as the leads.id pin already does: `Equals<SelectType<Database[t][c]>, string | null>` for the 8 nullable columns (alerts.premium_at_risk; leads.competitor_premium/estimated_premium/sum_insured; pricing_approvals.proposed_premium; quotes.bound_premium/competitor_premium; tenant_settings.high_value_threshold) and `Equals<SelectType<Database['quote_versions']['quoted_premium']>, string>` for the NOT NULL one. This closes both drift directions (mutant NA `? string` goes red at the 8 nullable pins; mutant NB `| null` goes red at quoted_premium) and makes the pin a true exact-type oracle with zero permitted variation - terminal for the select-type axis. Update the in-file comment (the 'nullability is the only permitted variation' claim becomes false) and extend the probe protocol with NA and NB. If a migration changes a column's nullability, the pin must be updated by hand alongside it - baseline failure will force this, which is the desired behaviour.
findings.resolution: Replaced the two-arm MoneyIsString (which accepted EITHER string or string|null for ANY column, so it never checked that the arm matched the column's real nullability) with exact per-column pins. Each column now states its own Select/Insert/Update types, so nullability is ASSERTED rather than permitted. Verified: probe P6 (`? Exclude<TValue,number>|string` -> `? string`, dropping null from all 8 nullable money selects) was a full four-gate survivor before and now fails typecheck (exit 2). Evaluator independently re-verified at iteration-5 re-review: P6 exit 2 with 9 semantic TS2322 kills (the 8 nullable pins on their Select arm PLUS quoteVersionsQuotedPremium via its Update arm, `string` vs `string | undefined`); pinned nullability audited against the live DB via information_schema (8 of 9 nullable, only quote_versions.quoted_premium NOT NULL, none defaulted) and against the generated supabase-types (nullable Insert/Update carry `?` optionality, hence the `| undefined`); restore cmp-byte-identical.
findings.summary: Fifth defeat of the money-type guarantee, on the NULLABILITY axis.

findings.description: Sixth defeat, on the INSERT/UPDATE axis. All pins cover ONLY the select side (SelectType). ApplyNumericOverride is deliberately applied to Insert and Update in kyselify.ts (the write path is where an IEEE-754 double premium would actually corrupt money in the database), but nothing pins that application: dropping the override from InsertType alone reverts every money column's INSERT type to the generator's `number` - future domain code would then be REQUIRED to pass doubles for premiums - and no gate goes red. No typed Kysely insert into any money-bearing table exists anywhere in src yet (grep verified: zero insertInto('leads'|'quotes'|'quote_versions'|'alerts'|'pricing_approvals'|'tenant_settings')), so nothing incidental catches it either; the iteration-4 'insert-side laundered any is killed' result relied on an any-mutant corrupting widely, not on any guard of the insert-side override specifically. UpdateType has the identical exposure.
findings.evidence: Evaluator probe at iteration-4 re-review, restored cmp+sha256-byte-identical (ad95c5ea...) afterwards. Mutant INS - InsertType's `? ApplyNumericOverride<T, K, BaseTables[T]['Insert'][K]>` -> `? BaseTables[T]['Insert'][K]` (override dropped from the insert path only; select and update untouched): FULL FOUR-GATE SURVIVOR - typecheck exit 0, lint exit 0, db:types:check exit 0, npm test 38 files / 594 passed / 0 skipped exit 0 - with every money column's insert type reverted to `number`. Reachability is weaker than F-008-5 (kyselify.ts is hand-written, so this needs a refactor slip rather than a generator regression), but the shared-helper structure is exactly what a future editor would 'simplify', and the task's own CRITICAL CATCH narrative ('parsing premiums into IEEE-754 doubles would silently corrupt money') describes the write path.
findings.suggested_fix: Add insert-side and update-side pins for the money columns mirroring the select block, using Kysely's exported InsertType/UpdateType utilities: expected insert type `string` for quote_versions.quoted_premium (required, NOT NULL, no default) and `string | null | undefined` for the 8 nullable defaulted columns (the `?` optionality flows through as `| undefined`, which is how Kysely spells optional-on-insert); update types analogous. Derive the exact expected shapes from the generated Insert/Update declarations and verify at baseline (a wrong expectation fails immediately, as the F-008-4 nullability correction demonstrated). Extend the probe protocol with: (a) override dropped from InsertType only -> red at the insert pins; (b) override dropped from UpdateType only -> red at the update pins. After F-008-5 + F-008-6, every money column is exactly pinned on all three of Select/Insert/Update with a strict Equals - the pin space on this guarantee is closed: vacuity (x3), sampling, nullability, and write-path axes all have demonstrated-red probes.
findings.resolution: Money pins now cover all THREE sides of ColumnType via Kysely's InsertType/UpdateType, not just SelectType, closing the write path where an IEEE-754 premium would actually corrupt stored money. Verified: probe P7 (ApplyNumericOverride dropped from the InsertType branch only) was a full four-gate survivor before and now fails typecheck (exit 2). NOTE ON METHOD: the true Insert/Update types were determined EMPIRICALLY, not guessed - a first attempt guessed Update as `string | null` and failed at baseline with 9 errors. A candidate-elimination probe (Eq<> against each candidate, reading which lines error) established the actual shapes: nullable money columns are Select `string|null`, Insert `string|null|undefined`, Update `string|null|undefined`; quote_versions.quoted_premium (the only NOT NULL money column) is Select `string`, Insert `string`, Update `string|undefined`. The `| undefined` on Update comes from Supabase update rows being all-optional - exactly what the guess missed. Evaluator independently re-verified at iteration-5 re-review: P7 exit 2 with 9 semantic TS2322 kills at all nine money pins (their Insert arms revert to the generator's number-bearing types); the empirical triples confirmed correct against the generated supabase-types (quoted_premium Insert required `number`, Update `?: number`; nullable columns `?: number | null` on both) and the live DB; a mirror probe dropping the override from the UpdateType branch only (the exposure named in this finding) also dies, exit 2 with 9 kills; restore cmp-byte-identical.
findings.summary: Sixth defeat, on the INSERT/UPDATE axis.

findings.description: db-types-drift.test.ts's first case ('regenerates types from the local schema with exit code 0') is the ONLY invocation of db:types WITHOUT --check anywhere in the suite: it physically REWRITES the committed generated artifacts (src/server/lib/db/generated/supabase-types.ts, column-overrides.ts) from live DB state — which at test time contains other suites' test-tenant partitions — and restores them only from an in-memory snapshot in a `finally`. Two failure modes leave the COMMITTED artifact corrupted on disk after the run: (a) interruption (crash/SIGKILL/timeout) between the write and the finally; (b) CONCURRENT runs of the suite — process B snapshots while process A's regenerated content is on disk, then B's 'restore' writes the polluted content back permanently even though both runs complete their finally blocks. (b) is exactly what happened when three implementors ran full suites in parallel: the first clean sequential run still failed 3 tests ('DB TYPE GENERATION FAILED'/drift), and only a manual `npm run db:types` against a clean DB repaired the committed files. This was NOT pure concurrency flake: the committed artifact had genuinely drifted and stayed drifted across runs. Downstream, T-008's compile-time guard and `npm run typecheck` depend on these files, so the corruption surfaces as unrelated-looking type failures with nothing pointing at the cause.
findings.evidence: src/server/tests/integration/db-types-drift.test.ts lines 61-79 (write-mode invocation + in-memory snapshot/finally restore; the test's own comment documents the partition-pollution mechanism and an observed untypecheckable tree). Orchestrator log: 3 drift-test failures on the first clean full run after parallel implementation, resolved only by manually running `npm run db:types`. Evaluator reproduced the healthy path 2026-07-20: db:types:check EXIT=0, suite green — the defect is a latent corruption window, not a currently red gate.
findings.suggested_fix: Never let a test write the committed artifact: add an --out <dir> option to scripts/db/generate-types.ts and point the write-mode test at a temp directory, asserting exit code (and optionally comparing temp output to committed via the same normalization --check uses). This removes both the interruption window and the cross-process interleaving, and incidentally decouples the test from partition pollution. If write-mode-in-place must stay, an on-disk snapshot restored by a process-exit handler plus an exclusive lock file is the weaker fallback.
findings.resolution: Fixed at the root by the orchestrator: generate-types.ts gains an `--out <dir>` flag, and the write-mode case in db-types-drift.test.ts now generates into a per-run mkdtemp directory instead of regenerating the COMMITTED artifacts and restoring them from an in-memory snapshot. This removes the corruption window rather than narrowing it - both failure modes the evaluator identified (interruption before the finally, and two concurrent runs interleaving so B restores A content permanently) are structurally impossible once the test never writes the real files. The test additionally asserts BOTH that generation genuinely happened in the temp dir (banner present) AND that the committed file is byte-identical afterwards, so the redirect silently ceasing to work cannot pass green. MUTATION PROVEN: making generatedDir ignore outDirArg() and always resolve to the committed directory - application verified semantically (grep for the outDirArg assignment returns 0; the line count was unchanged, so a line-count check alone would NOT have proven application here) - turns the suite red at exactly that case, 1 failed / 5 passed. Restored byte-identical; db:types:check exit 0. Gates after fix: npm test 58 files / 938 passed / 0 skipped exit 0, typecheck 0 run AFTER the full test (the exact order this defect used to break), lint 0, db:types:check 0. NOTE ON PROCESS: T-008 was left at PASS rather than reopened, because its PASS covered the data-layer type contract and this defect is in a test-harness write path; the fix is orchestrator-verified only, so it is queued for a focused evaluator re-check in the next evaluation round rather than being credited as independently confirmed. EVALUATOR INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION (2026-07-20 focused re-check): fix verified on its merits; see the evaluated_note history entry of the same date. The 'orchestrator-verified only' caveat is hereby discharged.

findings.description: Residual, narrower instance of the F-008-7 corruption-window class: the two 'DETECTS DRIFT' cases in db-types-drift.test.ts (lines 98-130) still write the COMMITTED generated artifacts in place (writeFileSync corruption + in-memory-snapshot restore in a finally). Much less severe than F-008-7's write-mode case: the corruption is a known deterministic token ('Drifted' line / 'not_a_column'), db:types:check immediately goes red naming the file, and `npm run db:types` repairs it - unlike the write-mode case, it cannot masquerade as valid regenerated content. Non-blocking; T-008 stays PASS.
findings.evidence: db-types-drift.test.ts:98-130 (both drift cases corrupt supabaseTypesPath/overridesPath directly). Feasibility of the fix proven first-hand by the evaluator: generate with `--out <tmp>`, corrupt the TEMP copy, then run `--check --out <tmp>` - clean copy exits 0, corrupted copy exits 1 - so drift detection can be exercised without ever touching the committed files (check-mode honours --out because writeOrCheck resolves all three paths under generatedDir).
findings.suggested_fix: Point the two drift cases at a per-run mkdtemp copy: `db:types --out <tmp>` to produce a baseline, corrupt the temp copy, assert `db:types --check --out <tmp>` exits 1 and names the file, then rmSync the temp dir. This removes the last test-side write to the committed artifacts, completing F-008-7's 'never let a test write the committed artifact' posture.
findings.resolution: Closed by the orchestrator immediately rather than deferred, because the evaluator had already proven the fix feasible (--check honours --out) and leaving a known corruption window open while more parallel tasks are about to run is exactly how F-008-7 reached production in the first place. Both DETECTS DRIFT cases now copy all three generated files into a per-run mkdtemp via a withGeneratedCopy helper, corrupt the COPY, and run `--check --out <tmp>`; the committed artifacts are never written. Each case additionally asserts a clean-copy baseline passes FIRST (so the expected failure is attributable to the corruption, not to the copy) and that all three committed files are byte-identical afterwards (so the redirect silently breaking cannot pass green). GENERATED_FILES covers tenant-scoped-tables.ts too, which --check also reads. MUTATION PROVEN, application shown semantically since the edit is same-line: replacing stale.push(path) with a no-op (stale.push count 1->0, marker 1) turns BOTH drift cases red (2 failed / 4 passed) - so the cases still genuinely detect drift and did not become vacuous by moving off the committed files. Restored (push count back to 1, zero markers). Gates: npm test 60 files / 1004 passed / 0 skipped exit 0; typecheck 0 AFTER the full run; lint 0; db:types:check 0; committed artifact sha256 unchanged across a full drift-suite run. This fix is ALSO orchestrator-verified only and is queued for the next evaluator round. Kysely data layer implemented. CODEGEN DECISION RESOLVED WITHOUT A NEW DEPENDENCY: `supabase gen types typescript --local` works and maps cleanly (its {Row,Insert,Update} triple is structurally ColumnType<Select,Insert,Update>; optional/identity encode as undefined in the union, exactly Kysely's encoding) via a pure-type adapter with zero runtime. kysely-codegen was NOT installed - orchestrator confirmed it is absent from devDependencies. `kysely@0.29.4` (MIT) was installed; it is on the spec-approved runtime list (Q-1/Q-2) but was missing from package.json. CRITICAL CATCH: the CLI types two column classes WRONG at runtime - `numeric` and `bigint` are declared as `number` but node-postgres returns STRING. Declaring premiums as number would have been a latent money bug seeded into every future domain task. Fixed with information_schema-generated overrides (not hand-listed) plus a pool-scoped int8 parser that THROWS above 2^53 rather than silently returning a different id. Pooler safety proved behaviourally with a positive control: prepared-statement sensor backed by a PREPARE-on-A/EXECUTE-on-B failure proving the hazard is real, so a green sensor cannot be vacuous; pool cap asserted against the live pool; rollback proven by asserting the earlier insert is ABSENT after both a thrown error and a constraint violation. Also documented that Kysely's AbortSignal cancellation uses pg_cancel_backend over a second connection and is unsafe under transaction pooling. TENANT DESIGN + STATED BYPASS: forTenant() pre-applies a parameterised predicate and injects tenant_id on insert (a caller-supplied one via `as` cast is overwritten, tested); TenantId is branded so a raw path param won't compile; TENANT_SCOPED_TABLES is generated from information_schema and cross-checked against the Kysely schema at COMPILE time. Bypass stated plainly and documented in tenant.ts: any caller can still write db.selectFrom('leads') unscoped - intentional, since cross-tenant Internal endpoints need it. It is a guard rail, not a sandbox; remaining layers are T-014 RLS, per-endpoint N-01 isolation tests, and reviewability. T-011's createPgAppUserLookup migrated to createDb behind the unchanged AppUserLookup port; auth suites 31 passed, no middleware changes. 7 mutants all killed, but the compile-time cross-check INITIALLY PASSED mutant 7 for two reasons - an unreferenced type alias is never instantiated, and a bare conditional type DISTRIBUTES so the failing member was absorbed into `true | never === true`; rewritten as a value-level [A] extends [B] assertion and re-verified red.

POST-PASS DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED (during T-016 remediation): scripts/db/generate-types.ts wrote `supabase gen types` output verbatim, and the CLI emits PARTITION tables.
